searchText: https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/issues/257 This is probably yet another reason to make CL capable of comparing the payout of external payload with the one that has been produced locally (0 bid is the edge case here). But for now it should be enough to check that the fee is greater than zero and fallback to local payload if it's not Yes, exactly. The public key is the user part of the URL (which is part of the spec https://www.w3.org/Addressing/URL/url-spec.txt (`<scheme>://<user>@<domain_name>:<port>/<path>`) and you can enter it like that in your browsers too). It's not pretty but gives additional security guarantees -- namely that proposers can verify that bids come from the actual trusted relay. Without the key, anyone taking over the URL could send bids, and configuring relays with pubkey ensures that a relay needs BOTH the DNS entry and the trusted secret key. Yes, it would be good to do these checks in the BN too. Added a PR for this for mev-boost too: https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/pull/261 But it's mainly the full nodes that matter, right? because soft fork?
